text:
maria gonzalez: quick thought — our current paging for GPU p95 blips is drowning the oncall rota.
raj singh: agree, we've been paged for ~20s flares that vanish. side effect: fatigue + ignored important pages.
sam kuo: +1. proposal: demote short-lived single-node spikes to tickets unless they meet additional conditions (sustained, cross-node, or impacting SLOs).
elaine park: what conditions are we thinking? sustained duration, cross-node correlation, and backing signal (OOM, evictions, queue length?)
maria gonzalez: exactly. my draft rule:
```
# Prometheus-ish pseudo-rule
ALERT GPU_Flare_High
IF node_gpu_utilization > 85
FOR 2m
LABELS { severity="page" }
ANNOTATIONS { summary="Sustained high GPU util" }

ALERT GPU_Flare_Short
IF node_gpu_utilization > 90
FOR 15s
LABELS { severity="ticket" }
ANNOTATIONS { summary="Short-lived GPU spike — ticket only" }
```
raj singh: i like having a short FOR to catch noise and mark ticket severity. also add a recording rule to compute node-level p95 over 5m and a cross-node correlate metric:
```
record: job:node_gpu_util:5m_p95
expr: quantile_over_time(0.95, node_gpu_utilization[5m])
```
sam kuo: and aggregation/grouping by labels is crucial — avoid high cardinality. group by (region, pool, gpu_model) so we can decide per-pool policies.
elaine park: Grafana action: add a panel that shows current ephemeral vs sustained page counts and a filter for "ticket-only spikes". useful during postmortems.
sre-bot: deploy-notice: alert-rules/gpu-spike-policy.yml will be applied to staging in 30m if no objections.
maria gonzalez: cost note — pages that auto-resolve still generate oncall context switch. demoting ~70% of these to tickets should save ~1.4 FTE-equivalent hours/month in interruption cost (rough calc).
raj singh: edge cases: single-node sustained at 100% with queue growth should still page even if only one node — add queue_length > threshold as an OR condition.
sam kuo: also consider region-wide capacity constraint: if >50% of nodes in an AZ show p95>80 concurrently => page immediately.
elaine park: runtime hysteresis: use FOR >2m for pages, but add a cool-off window so we don't re-page on rapid flapping (suppress repeat pages for same group for 30m).
maria gonzalez: next steps: 1) update prometheus rules PR with the ticket/page labels + recordings, 2) create Grafana panel + dashboard annotation, 3) run it in staging for 48h, 4) review oncall noise metrics and decide rollback threshold.
raj singh: I'll draft the PR and include example runbook sections for ticket vs page handling.
sam kuo: i'll add grouping and low-cardinality labels to the node-exporter relabel config to keep metrics sane.
elaine park: thanks all — if no objections, let's let the bot push to staging and monitor.
maria gonzalez: no objections from me. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: deploy-complete: rules applied to staging cluster at 2234010476. monitor: grafana/dashboard/gpu-noise -> panel 5.
raj singh: recording results will be visible in the new dashboard. feel free to poke me if you see weird regressions.
